Feature Big Tech Discovers America Companies like Apple, Alphabet, and Tesla are increasingly moving operations to places like Reno, Nev., in search of cheaper land and easier living. By March 15, 2018 8:27 a.m. ET By Jon Swartz March 15, 2018 8:27 a.m. ET 
RENO, Nev.—Nevada Gov. Brian Sandoval had reason to beam and boast at a tech show here recently. 
The city of 300,000 he affectionately calls “Silicon Bridge” for its proximity to San Francisco—about 218 miles—has emerged as a capital of big tech investments. From Tesla’s (ticker: TSLA) 5.8-million-square-foot Gigafactory and Apple’s (AAPL) sprawling new $4 million warehouse downtown, to Amazon.com’s (AMZN) 630,000-square-foot fulfillment center on the north end of town and Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Google expansion efforts, Reno...
